name: The Perceptron
description: Rosenblatt's single-layer network — the first machine that could learn from examples.

name: Backpropagation
description: The chain-rule algorithm that lets errors flow backward through a network to update its weights.

name: Convolutional Neural Networks
description: LeCun's LeNet taught networks to see, sliding small filters across pixels to find edges, shapes, digits.

name: RNNs and LSTMs
description: Networks with memory: recurrent connections and the LSTM's gates let models handle sequences.

name: Support Vector Machines
description: A geometric approach to classification: find the widest possible margin between classes.

name: The ImageNet Moment
description: AlexNet crushed the 2012 ImageNet competition, kicking off the deep learning boom.

name: Word Embeddings
description: word2vec packed word meaning into dense vectors — king minus man plus woman equals queen.

name: Generative Adversarial Networks
description: Two networks locked in a contest — a forger and a detective — learn to generate strikingly realistic data.

name: The Attention Mechanism
description: Letting a model look back at every input token and weigh what matters most, however far away.

name: The Transformer
description: "Attention Is All You Need" — dropping recurrence entirely reshaped every corner of machine learning.

name: Large Language Models
description: Scaling transformers to billions of parameters and web-scale data produced fluent, general-purpose foundation models.
